hypothesis: Phase 2 cost-ceiling bracket: raw full-history prompting (llm-fullhistory) versus a typed, queryable AKG graph (llm-akg-durable), heads-up and NON-mirror, seat-mirrored across seeds so positional and blind-rotation effects cancel. This is the bottom of the cost axis: llm-fullhistory stuffs every prior hand back into the prompt, so per-decision input tokens grow O(N) and the prompt balloons as the session runs - a prior 200-hand run was prohibitively expensive. The horizon is deliberately SHORT (80 hands) to capture the linear token-growth slope and the early part of the curve without the runaway cost; if it hits the context ceiling first, that hand count IS the result. Reported on the FIDELITY-VS-COST FRONTIER, not chips: AKG's precomputed-profile reads stay roughly flat while full-history climbs linearly; full-history fidelity is high in principle (the raw transcript is lossless) but the model must re-derive everything in-context every decision. Chip outcomes are DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Both agents are built, so this rung is runnable now.
